headline: Visa and Mastercard signed on as launch partners to Stripe's Machine Payments Protocol, a standard on its Tempo blockchain that lets AI agents pay for services without a person approving each payment.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 by 2: the launch it describes happened on 18 Mar 2026, so this is a recap of old news, and much of it is the outlet's opinion about why the card networks joined.
importance_line: Shoppers and businesses may later let AI agents pay on their behalf, which touches the card networks first and Stripe and its partners next, and the doubt is that Startup Fortune's view that Visa and Mastercard joined to hedge against stablecoins (digital money pegged to a real currency) is analysis, not something either company said.
summary: Startup Fortune reports that Stripe's Tempo blockchain launched with the Machine Payments Protocol, an open standard that lets AI agents authorise and make payments on their own, with Visa and Mastercard among its launch partners, and argues that they joined so as not to be left out if agents prefer cheaper stablecoin payments. The piece recaps the launch of 18 Mar 2026 and adds that Mastercard separately agreed to buy stablecoin firm BVNK for up to $1.8 billion and that Visa has a closed-beta tool, Visa CLI, for agent card payments.
notes: Read in full from the main session's fulltext copy. Event date 18 Mar 2026 (year inferred from context; the article says only 'March 18'). Mostly recap and opinion; no new event dated on or after 11 Oct 2026 was found in the text.
